pairs.evidence: lib/notebook/corpus.ts:102 The corpus gate groups and snapshots refusals by rule keys it rebuilds from the finding sentences with regexes, because graph.ts writes the typed GraphIssue kind into the `rule` prose and NotebookFinding has no kind field; rewording a rule changes approved verdicts, and one cause can split across several wordings.

techniques.evidence: lib/notebook/graph.ts:72 The typed GraphIssue kind is turned into a message prefix at the boundary and does not survive as a field.
lib/notebook/corpus.ts:54 The gate classifies findings by regex over prose (`[kind]` prefix, digit and quote stripping), not by a structured field.
lib/notebook/failure.ts:17 Findings carry a machine `path` that the repair turn branches on; the route maps the failure to the existing `bad-response` code instead of adding a second vocabulary.
lib/notebook/validate.ts:112 A notebook is one document, so the whole document is refused, with every finding addressed by its path and the draft kept.
lib/notebook/corpus.ts:100 Only the expected refusal is absorbed into a verdict; anything else is rethrown, not swallowed.
lib/notebook/shape.ts:162 A probe that does not compile becomes a path-addressed finding that carries the thrown message; it is not dropped.

techniques.evidence: packages/domain/src/door.ts:52 The field path, which is category-specific data, is flattened into the message instead of travelling as a field.
